whatItIs.text: Rice milled to remove the bran and germ — the fluffy long-grain or sticky short-grain staple of over half the world's population.

historyNote.text: Asian rice was domesticated in China some 13,500-8,200 years ago, and African rice independently in West Africa about 3,000 years ago; the black 'forbidden rice' variety was once reserved for the royal family in ancient China.

howToChoose.text: Long-grain for separate fluffy grains (pilafs, fried rice), short-grain for stickiness (sushi, rice pudding); basmati and jasmine bring aroma for free.

storage.text: Keep dry and sealed in a cool cupboard; cooked rice needs prompt cooling and refrigeration.

foodSafetyRef.note: Storage claims backed by food-safety rulebook rules: two-hour-rule, cool-rapidly-shallow-containers.

useItUp.text: Day-old rice is fried rice's requirement, not its problem; leftover rice also bakes into rice pudding, thickens soup, or crisps into patties.

substitutions.note: nuttier, chewier; more water and time
